question:
Assertion (A): The relation $R$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ defined by $aRb \Leftrightarrow a-b \in \mathbb{Q}$ is an equivalence relation.

Reason (R): For all $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$, $a-b$ is always rational.
explanation:
Check Assertion (A): The relation $R$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ is defined by $aRb \Leftrightarrow a-b \in \mathbb{Q}$.

Reflexive: $a-a = 0 \in \mathbb{Q}$, so the relation is reflexive.

Symmetric: If $a-b \in \mathbb{Q}$ then $b-a = -(a-b) \in \mathbb{Q}$, so it is symmetric.

Transitive: If $a-b \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $b-c \in \mathbb{Q}$ then $a-c = (a-b) + (b-c) \in \mathbb{Q}$, so it is transitive.

Thus the Assertion is true.

Check Reason (R): Since $\mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{Q}$, the difference of two integers is always rational.

Therefore the Reason is also true and correctly explains the Assertion.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
